page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ine.4xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server instance within the Enhanced family, hosted on the KVM hypervisor. The instance features 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. System memory totals 64.0 GB, providing an even allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, matching standard 1:4 compute-to-memory architecture requirements.

The hardware configuration includes 23 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage for persistent data requirements. The instance does not include hardware accelerators or graphics processing units, maintaining a focus on core compute and network throughput. Zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

From an infrastructure perspective, the dedicated CPU allocation and substantial 23 Gbps baseline networking support consistent execution without resource contention from burst credit mechanisms. The absence of bundled local storage introduces reliance on remote network-attached disks, which trades local low-latency disk IO for flexible storage provisioning. The hardware profile suits network-heavy backend services, enterprise application deployments, containerized clusters, and multi-tier web architectures.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8ine.4xlarge is a general-purpose server instance belonging to the Enhanced family, built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor operating at 2.7 GHz, paired with 64.0 GB of memory to yield a 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned at a 23 Gbps baseline, and the system operates without bundled local NVMe storage or discrete GPU accelerators. Because persistent storage relies entirely on external volumes, disk performance depends on network-attached storage configurations. With dedicated processor cores and high networking bandwidth, the configuration provides predictable execution for distributed applications, enterprise middleware, API gateways, and production web serving.
